---
title: Build a Raycast extension
description: Write a small Raycast extension that saves a link to your instance, with a key of its own that can write bookmarks and nothing else.
---

- **You'll build** a Raycast extension with one command. It shows a form for a link, and saves what you type to your instance as a bookmark.
- **You need** your own Marfa instance, with the CLI signed in to it, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you, plus [Raycast](https://www.raycast.com) and [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.22.2 or later on a Mac.
- **You'll have** a command that saves links from anywhere on your Mac. [Build forms from types in a Raycast extension](/build/raycast-type-forms) builds on it.

An extension is a client of your instance, like any app you write. It sends requests with a key, and the key decides what it may do. Here the key can write bookmarks and nothing else.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Make a key for the extension

A key is the credential a program sends with each request. Give the extension a key of its own, so that it reaches only what it needs. In a terminal, make a key that reads and writes bookmarks:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa keys create --label "Raycast" --source raycast \
  --type-permission core.bookmark=write
```

```text
marfa_k1_…
key 01a1f142-25ea-7671-bd26-35207a9efab1 (Raycast); the plaintext is shown once, keep it now
  core.bookmark  Read and edit
```

</Terminal>

<Callout type="warn" title="Copy the key now">Marfa shows it once. If you lose it, make a new one.</Callout>

The **source** is the label Marfa puts on every item the key creates, so you can always tell what the extension saved. The `--type-permission` flag names the one type the key may write. [Manage keys](/run/manage-keys) explains each flag, and [Access](/build/access) explains what a key can hold.

</Step>
<Step>

### Create the extension and add the client

Open Raycast and run the **Create Extension** command. Name the extension "Marfa Capture", pick any template, since step 4 replaces its code, and choose a folder. Then, in the new folder, add the Marfa client:

```bash
npm install @withmarfa/client
```

The [TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk) is a typed client for every operation. It knows each path, parameter and answer, so a mistake in a request fails to build.

The client is an ES module, and the template's `tsconfig.json` compiles for CommonJS, which can't find it. In `tsconfig.json`, set `module` to `preserve`, so that TypeScript resolves the client the way Raycast's bundler does:

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "preserve"
  }
}
```

Leave the template's other options as they are.

The extension needs to know where your instance is and which key to use. In `package.json`, set the command's `title` and `description`, and add two **preferences**. Raycast asks for them the first time the command runs, and hides a `password` preference:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "platforms": ["macOS"],
  "commands": [
    {
      "name": "index",
      "title": "Save Link",
      "description": "Save a link to Marfa",
      "mode": "view"
    }
  ],
  "preferences": [
    {
      "name": "apiUrl",
      "title": "Server URL",
      "description": "Where your Marfa instance answers",
      "type": "textfield",
      "required": true,
      "default": "http://localhost:8600"
    },
    {
      "name": "apiKey",
      "title": "API Key",
      "description": "A key made for this extension",
      "type": "password",
      "required": true
    }
  ]
}
```

The command's `name` matches the file `src/index.tsx`. Leave the rest of the template's `package.json` as it is.

</Step>
<Step>

### Keep every call in one module

Put each request to Marfa in one file. The rest of the extension then asks for a saved item, and never sees a URL or a key:

```ts title="src/marfa.ts"
import { getPreferenceValues } from "@raycast/api";
import { createClient } from "@withmarfa/client";

/** What the server said when it refused a request. */
export class MarfaError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    readonly code: string,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
  }
}

function client() {
  const { apiUrl, apiKey } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
  return createClient({ baseUrl: apiUrl.trim(), credential: apiKey.trim() });
}

type Refusal = { error: { code: string; message: string } };

function refused(response: Response, refusal: Refusal) {
  return new MarfaError(response.status, refusal.error.code, refusal.error.message);
}

export async function createItem(type: string, properties: Record<string, unknown>) {
  const { data, error, response } = await client().POST("/items", {
    body: { type, properties },
  });
  if (error) throw refused(response, error);
  return data.item;
}
```

[Create an item](/api-reference/items/createItem) returns `data` when it works and `error` when Marfa refuses it. A refusal carries a stable `code` and a `message` for people, so `MarfaError` keeps both. `Preferences` is a type Raycast generates from the `package.json` you edited, so don't write it yourself.

</Step>
<Step>

### Build the form and save the link

A bookmark is an item of the type `core.bookmark`. A **type** is the shape of an item: it lists the fields the item holds. A bookmark holds a `url`, a `title` and `notes`, among others. Replace `src/index.tsx` with a form for those three fields:

```tsx title="src/index.tsx"
import { Action, ActionPanel, Form, popToRoot, showToast, Toast } from "@raycast/api";
import { createItem, MarfaError } from "./marfa";

export default function SaveLink() {
  async function save(values: Form.Values) {
    const properties = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(values).filter(([, value]) => value !== ""));
    try {
      const item = await createItem("core.bookmark", properties);
      await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Success, title: "Saved", message: item.id });
      await popToRoot();
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof MarfaError) {
        await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Failure, title: `Refused: ${error.code}`, message: error.message });
      } else {
        await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Failure, title: "Could not reach Marfa", message: String(error) });
      }
    }
  }

  return (
    <Form
      actions={
        <ActionPanel>
          <Action.SubmitForm title="Save to Marfa" onSubmit={save} />
        </ActionPanel>
      }
    >
      <Form.TextField id="url" title="URL" placeholder="https://" />
      <Form.TextField id="title" title="Title" />
      <Form.TextArea id="notes" title="Notes" />
    </Form>
  );
}
```

Each control's `id` is the name of the field it fills. `save` leaves out a field left empty, so the bookmark holds no value for it, and shows the server's `code` and `message` when Marfa refuses it. The bookmark arrives with the `source` of the key, `raycast`. [Bookmark](/catalog/bookmark) lists every field the type holds.

</Step>
<Step>

### Run the extension

In the extension's folder, start it:

```bash
npm run dev
```

It builds the extension, adds it to Raycast and rebuilds it each time you save a file. If it reports a type error, the message names the file and line.

Open Raycast and search for **Save Link**. The first time, Raycast asks for the preferences. The server URL is filled in with `http://localhost:8600`; change it if your instance answers elsewhere, and paste the key from step 1. Enter a URL and a title, and press Command-Return. A **Saved** toast shows the new bookmark's ID.

Check the bookmark in the terminal, with the CLI's own key:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items list --source raycast
```

```text
id                                    type           when                      title
01a1f142-4174-75ec-9281-22401f2a0c56  core.bookmark  2026-11-19T00:43:33.620Z  Great Expectations on Project Gutenberg
```

</Terminal>

You now have a Raycast command that saves links to your own instance, with a key that can do little else. Stop `npm run dev` in the terminal when you're done. The extension stays in Raycast.

</Step>
</Steps>
